summary: Made the one untested consequence channel explicit without claiming it. Two source-grounded entries were added: a leader accepts a client membership change as soon as its own latest configuration is committed and it has committed an entry in its term, then computes the new configuration from configurations.latest, installs it immediately and rebuilds its commitment from it (the request's prevIndex being the only guard, with the package's own AddPeer and RemovePeer helpers passing 0); and, because of that, the quorum committing such a change is the reconstructed one rather than the committed configuration's quorum, so with a smaller reconstruction the change can be committed with support that is not a majority of the configuration being replaced, can include a peer that configuration does not contain, and never asks the peers the reconstruction no longer counts. I registered the matching necessary gap (does a client change issued to a reconstruction-governed leader produce a committed configuration the previous majority never agreed to, and what do the demoted peers observe and adopt?), updated the question's discriminator to that channel, and appended a question-level supplement with conclusion and defect judgment unresolved that explicitly keeps the exercised account intact under its receipts. No execution was spent; the channel is source-reasoned only, and the peers' adoption and any concurrent leadership among disjoint configurations are deliberately left unclaimed.
